key_insights.finding: Cerium posted the biggest price gain of any mineral in the dataset.
key_insights.evidence: Up 80.0% from 2015 to 2026, per the annual global price series.
key_insights.interpretation: Cerium outpaced all 24 tracked minerals over the period.

key_insights.finding: Nothing actually lost value over 2015-2026 -- Nickel just gained the least.
key_insights.evidence: Nickel rose 5.0%, the smallest increase of any of the 24 minerals. Every mineral's full-period change is positive.
key_insights.interpretation: Nickel was the weakest performer here, but weakest still means it went up, not down -- worth keeping straight before calling anything a decliner.

key_insights.finding: Lithium is the most volatile mineral in the dataset.
key_insights.evidence: Coefficient of variation of 80.16% over 2015-2026 -- the highest of any mineral tracked.
key_insights.interpretation: That's a measure of how much the price swung around historically, not a forecast of future risk.

market_signals.finding: 25 mineral-country-year rows carry an active export control, mostly in the last few years.
market_signals.evidence: Every flagged row traces back to China (rare earths, gallium, germanium, graphite) or the DRC (cobalt).
market_signals.interpretation: Export-control activity in this dataset sits with a handful of dominant producing countries, not spread broadly.

market_signals.finding: hhi and top_country_share_pct move together more closely than any other pair of variables in the dataset.
market_signals.interpretation: Statistical association only -- see the Correlations page for the full matrix and the usual causation caveat.

risks_to_monitor.finding: Gallium carries the highest average supply-risk score in the dataset.
risks_to_monitor.evidence: Average supply_risk_score of 77.59 across all recorded years.
risks_to_monitor.interpretation: That score is driven by production concentration (HHI, top-country share), not by price behavior.

opportunities.finding: Copper has the steadiest historical pricing of any mineral tracked.
opportunities.evidence: Coefficient of variation of 8.5%, the lowest in the dataset.
opportunities.interpretation: For planning that values predictability over upside, that stability is the relevant signal -- based only on the price series observed here.

recommended_investigation.finding: Price barely tracks mine production or reserve size in this dataset.
recommended_investigation.evidence: Pearson r between price_usd_per_tonne and mine_production_tonnes = -0.09.
recommended_investigation.interpretation: So price here isn't just a function of how much gets mined. What actually drives it isn't in these columns -- that would take outside market data to dig into.

recommended_investigation.finding: All 7 rare-earth minerals show an identical +80.0% price change over the full period, while everything else ranges from +5% to +48%.
recommended_investigation.evidence: Cerium, Dysprosium, Lanthanum, Neodymium, Praseodymium, Terbium, and Yttrium each land on exactly +80.0% from 2015 to 2026.
recommended_investigation.interpretation: That's too clean to be a real market coincidence -- more likely an artifact of how the source price series was built than an actual shared market event. Worth checking against the generation methodology or real prices before treating it as a signal.
